# Plan: Doku neu ordnen, alles auf Englisch, starkes README

## Context

Das Produkt ist fertig. Die Doku ist aber gemischt: README auf Englisch, der Rest
(`docs/ARCHITEKTUR.md`, `docs/DEPLOY.md`, `docs/REPO_CHECK.md`, `src/shared/API.md`,
`data/README.md`, `config/README.md`, `scripts/README.md`, `src/README.md`) auf Deutsch.
`src/frontend/README.md` ist noch der Next.js-Standardtext. Es gibt nur zwei Bilder
(`visuals/app/cockpit.png`, `visuals/techflow.png`). Ein Product Manager oder Jurymitglied
findet keinen klaren Einstieg, der erklärt, was ReSpec ist, wie man es benutzt und warum
man dem Ergebnis trauen kann.

Ziel: Eine saubere, englische Doku mit klarem Einstieg. Ein README, das in 30 Sekunden
überzeugt (Bilder, Workflow, Zahlen), und darunter kurze Dokumente für Produkt/PM,
Technik und Betrieb.

**Schreibstil für alle neuen Texte** (Vorgabe von Piyush): natürlich, direkt, kurze Sätze,
einfache präzise Wörter, keine Floskeln, kein Marketing-Sprech, keine Gedankenstriche als
Stilmittel. Klingt wie ein kluger Student, der etwas klar erklärt. Nach dem Schreiben
jede Datei einmal mit dem Skill `humanizer` gegenlesen.

**Nicht im Umfang:** Code, Code-Kommentare, Tests, Team-Regeln. `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`
und `.claude/skills/` bleiben deutsch (internes Team-Werkzeug), nur Links werden angepasst.

## Wichtige Randbedingung: EHL-Budget

CI prüft mit `python scripts/ehl_budget.py --pruefen`, dass Doku höchstens 25 % des
Review-Budgets (~200.000 Zeichen) belegt. Mehr Doku kann CI rot machen.
Lösung: README und `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` bleiben im Zipball (die Review-KI soll sie lesen).
Die längeren Produkt-Dokumente kommen nach `docs/product/` und `docs/images/`;
falls das Budget reißt, bekommen sie `export-ignore` in `.gitattributes` (auf GitHub
bleiben sie sichtbar). Nach jedem Schritt Budget messen.

## Neue Struktur

```
README.md                      Schaufenster (neu geschrieben)
docs/
  README.md                    Index: welches Dokument für wen
  product/
    OVERVIEW.md                Problem, Nutzer, Wert, End-to-End-Workflow (für PMs)
    PM_GUIDE.md                So benutzt ein PM das Cockpit, Bildschirm für Bildschirm
    PRIORITIZATION.md          Score-Formel, Faktoren, Gewichte, Evidenzstufen A-D
    GLOSSARY.md                Evidence, Finding/Signal, Requirement, Scenario, Bundle ...
  ARCHITECTURE.md              ersetzt ARCHITEKTUR.md (englisch, gekürzt, gegliedert)
  EVALUATION.md                Eval-Zahlen aller 6 Szenarien + Methode + Grenzen
                               (ersetzt inhaltlich REPO_CHECK.md)
  DEPLOY.md                    englisch (lokal, Render + Vercel, Tunnel, Checkliste)
  images/                      neue Screenshots + Diagramme
src/shared/API.md              englisch übersetzt, Pfad bleibt (wird im Code referenziert)
data/README.md, config/README.md, scripts/README.md, src/README.md   englisch
src/frontend/README.md         echtes README fürs Cockpit statt Next.js-Vorlage
```

Alte deutsche Dateien `docs/ARCHITEKTUR.md` und `docs/REPO_CHECK.md` werden durch die
englischen ersetzt (Git-Historie behält sie). Verweise anpassen in: `CLAUDE.md`,
`src/README.md`, `.claude/skills/challenge-intake/SKILL.md`,
`.claude/skills/demo-check/SKILL.md`, `render.yaml`, `tests/pfad_b/test_deploy_cors.py`
(nur Kommentar). Code-Dateien, die `API.md` erwähnen, brauchen keine Änderung, weil der
Pfad gleich bleibt.

## Inhalt je Datei

### 1. README.md (Schaufenster)
Reihenfolge, damit ein Leser oben schon alles Wichtige hat:

96	bereitgestellten Optionsliste: `source`, `reference_market` (Germany), `currency`

99	Referenz gilt nicht als US-/CN-Preis oder als Kostenschaetzung fuer den Nachfolger.
100	`engines` bezeichnet Antriebsarten in vorhandenen Belegen, nicht das vollstaendige

106	**Neu (Welle 2, alle mit Default):** `horizon` (`today|next_gen`), `robustness` (`{rank_min, rank_max, top3_share, runs}` oder null),
107	`segment_conflicts` (`[{dimension, segment_a, segment_b, statement, a_count, b_count, evidence_ids}]`),
108	`business` (`{volume_2025, volume_2030, growth_pct, market_share, note}` oder null; null-Werte = „nicht verfügbar“),

116	`ice_critical_share`, `ice_scenario_share` (Anteile 0–1), `evidence_ids`, `signal_ids`,

1	"""Evidenzstufe A-D: feste Regeln statt LLM-Bauchgefühl (Owner: Pfad C).
2	
3	Warum Regeln: Der Brief will klar sehen, wo eine Aussage auf Belegen beruht und wo
4	auf Annahmen. Eine Regel ist prüfbar und für den PM in einem Satz erklärbar.
5	
6	Die Regel in einem Satz (Entscheidung Sa 10.10., kalibriert an den echten G60-US-Daten):
7	  Basis nur nach Nennungen (15+ = B, sonst C); bestätigt eine zweite, unabhängige Quellenart
8	  die Aussage (mindestens 5 Nennungen), steigt die Stufe um eine (B -> A, C -> B). Auf A hebt nur
9	  eine zweite BMW-Quelle; Web hebt höchstens auf B.
10	
11	Echte Zahlen (G60-US, 16 Anforderungen, Nennungen von 7 bis 581): Nur 6 sind durch eine Studie
12	bestätigt. Mit der alten Regel (A = zwei Quellenarten UND 20 Nennungen) gab es 1 x A, 12 x B, 3 x C,
13	und eine Spracherkennung mit 8 Nennungen plus Studie (16 % unzufrieden) stand gleichauf mit einer
14	Vermutung. Jetzt: 3 x A, 13 x B. Verworfen: A schon ab 10 Nennungen (Schwelle schwer zu begründen,
15	setzt eine kleine Anforderung vor den Touchscreen mit 161 Nennungen).
16	Viele Nennungen aus EINER Quelle ergeben nie A: Die Stufe sagt, wie sicher wir sind, und eine Quelle
17	kann sich irren.
18	
19	Nachkalibrierung mit Webbelegen (Sa 10.10. abends): Mit Webrecherche standen beim G60-US 10 von 12
20	Anforderungen auf A (F70-EU 9 von 16), weil fast jede einen Webtreffer hat, und der streift oft nur das
21	Thema (z. B. Kofferraumvolumen eines Wettbewerbers als "Beleg" für ein Türschloss-Problem). Darum hebt
22	Web nur bis B; A braucht zwei BMW-eigene Quellen (Feedback + Studie), passend zur Mentor-Aussage
23	"BMW-Daten > Web". Ergebnis: G60-US 4 x A, F70-EU 3 x A. Verworfen: Web gar nicht mehr zählen lassen
24	(dann wäre die Triangulation wertlos und ein dünner Befund mit Webbestätigung bliebe C).
25	"""
26	
27	from __future__ import annotations
28	
29	from core.models import EvidenceLevel, SourceType
30	
31	# Unabhängige Quellenarten. Absatz und Optionsliste sind Kontext, kein Kundenbeleg.
32	CUSTOMER_SOURCES = {SourceType.FEEDBACK, SourceType.STUDY, SourceType.WEB}
33	
34	# Rangfolge laut BMW-Mentor: BMW-eigene Daten zählen mehr als Web/Social Media. Die
35	# Feedback-Quellen A-D untereinander sind gleichwertig, darum gibt es dafür keine Regel.
36	# Web darf bestätigen (zweite Quellenart), aber allein nie eine Anforderung tragen.
37	BMW_SOURCES = {SourceType.FEEDBACK, SourceType.STUDY}
38	
39	SOLID_MENTIONS = 15  # ab hier ist ein Thema mit einer Quelle belastbar genug für B
40	MIN_MENTIONS_FOR_LIFT = 5  # darunter hebt auch eine Bestätigung nicht: zu dünn, um mehr als Zufall zu sein
41	
42	
43	def classify(
44	    mention_count: int, source_types: set[SourceType], forward_looking: bool,
45	    next_gen: bool = False, customer_mentions: int = 0,
46	) -> tuple[EvidenceLevel, str]:
47	    """Liefert Stufe + Begründungssatz (englisch, steht im Wasserfall für den PM).
48	
49	    next_gen = Wette auf den Nachfolger (W-C3): Trends und Webtreffer zählen hier nicht als Kundenbeleg.
50	    Tragen weniger als 15 direkte Kundennennungen (customer_mentions) die Wette, ist sie eine Annahme: D.
51	    """
52	    independent = source_types & CUSTOMER_SOURCES
53	    if next_gen and customer_mentions < SOLID_MENTIONS:
54	        return EvidenceLevel.D, (f"Bet on the next generation: only {customer_mentions} direct customer mentions, "
55	                                 "the rest rests on trends (assumption).")
56	    if forward_looking and mention_count < 5:
57	        return EvidenceLevel.D, "Forward-looking assumption: few direct customer data points, rests on trends."
58	    if not independent:
59	        return EvidenceLevel.C, "No customer data behind it: at most a hint."
60	    if not independent & BMW_SOURCES:
61	        return EvidenceLevel.C, f"{mention_count} mentions from web sources only: without BMW data at most a hint."
62	    solid = mention_count >= SOLID_MENTIONS
63	    confirmed = len(independent) >= 2 and mention_count >= MIN_MENTIONS_FOR_LIFT
64	    bmw_confirmed = len(independent & BMW_SOURCES) >= 2  # nur Feedback + Studie reicht für A
65	    if solid and confirmed and bmw_confirmed:
66	        return EvidenceLevel.A, f"{mention_count} mentions, confirmed by {len(independent)} independent source types."
67	    if solid and confirmed:
68	        return EvidenceLevel.B, (f"{mention_count} mentions, confirmed only by web sources: "
69	                                 "A needs a second BMW source (study).")
70	    if confirmed:
71	        return EvidenceLevel.B, (f"Only {mention_count} mentions, but confirmed by {len(independent)} "
72	                                 "independent source types.")
73	    if solid:
74	        return EvidenceLevel.B, f"{mention_count} mentions, but from a single source type."
75	    return EvidenceLevel.C, f"Only {mention_count} mentions: a hint, not a solid finding."

13	|---|---|---|
14	| Grounding Befunde: zitierte Beleg-IDs, die existieren | 100.0 % | 100 % |
15	| Grounding Anforderungen: zitierte Befund-IDs, die existieren | 100.0 % | 100 % |
16	| Wortlaut: zitierte Kommentare, wörtlich in der Excel | 100.0 % | 100 % |

21	## Methode
22	
23	- **Grounding/Wortlaut:** automatisch aus den erzeugten Dateien und der Original-Excel, jede ID einzeln geprüft.
24	- **Befund-Treue:** 50 zufällige Paare (Befund, zitierter Beleg), Seed 42, mit j/n gelabelt
25	  ("belegt der Kommentar die Aussage des Befunds?"). Ablauf offen benannt: Claude schlug pro Paar j/n mit
26	  Begründung vor, ein Teammitglied (Aditya) prüfte die Liste und bestätigte sie; die Zahl stammt also nicht
27	  allein von der KI, ist aber auch kein blindes Menschenurteil. Ein zweiter Durchlauf (KI-Vorlabel, von Lasse
28	  alle 50 Zeilen geprüft und bestätigt) kam ebenfalls auf 88 %, mit teils anderen Nein-Fällen.
29	- **Abdeckung:** Kommentare im Umfang (ohne Werkstattfälle), die zu einer Gruppe eines ausgegebenen Befunds gehören.
30	- **Akzeptanzkriterium mit Zahl:** mindestens eine Ziffer im Text. Das ist ein Näherungswert für "messbar".
31	
32	## Grenzen
33	
34	- 50 Paare, Menschen prüften KI-Vorschläge (kein Blind-Label): grobe Größenordnung, kein Konfidenzintervall.
35	- Befund-Treue mit KI-Vorschlag: Ankereffekt möglich; blindes Zweitlabel durch einen Menschen wäre der nächste
36	  Schritt.

# ReSpec **Respect the voice. Define the spec.** ReSpec reads thousands of customer comments about a BMW and turns them into a ranked list of requirements for the next model. Every requirement links back to the customers who said it. The AI drafts. A product manager decides. Every decision is logged. We built it in 24 hours at the TUM.ai × EHL Grand Finale 2026 for the BMW Group challenge *"AI for Product Decision Making"*. [![CI](https://github.com/PiyushPapaya/TUMHackathon26/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/PiyushPapaya/TUMHackathon26/actions/workflows/ci.yml) ![Python 3.12](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.12-3776ab) ![FastAPI](https://img.shields.io/badge/backend-FastAPI-009688) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/frontend-Next.js-black) ![ReSpec start page](docs/images/home.jpg) --- ## Why we built this BMW gave us the raw material a product manager actually works with: 3,610 customer comments on the 5 Series in the US, a customer satisfaction study, sales forecasts up to 2030 and the official option list. The question behind it is simple. **What does the next 5 Series need to do better, and how sure are we?** Answering that by hand means reading for weeks. You end up with a slide that says "customers want better climate controls", and nobody can tell anymore whether that came from 300 people or from three loud ones. We have all seen decisions like that get made on gut feeling. So we set ourselves three rules: 1. **Every claim has to point to real customers.** If the AI cannot cite a comment, the claim is gone. 2. **The ranking has to be explainable in one sentence.** No black box score. Plain math you can redo. 3. **A human makes the call.** The AI proposes. Only the PM approves, rejects or edits, and has to say why. ReSpec is what came out of that. --- ## How it works ```mermaid flowchart LR V["3,610 customer
comments"] --> E["Evidence
with stable IDs"] S["Study, sales,
option list"] --> E W["Web sources
with URL + date"] --> F E --> F["58 findings
(what customers keep saying)"] F --> R["19 requirements
(what the successor must do)"] R --> P["Priority score
(plain formula)"] P --> D{"PM decides
approve / reject / edit / challenge"} D --> A[("Audit trail
hash chain")] classDef ai fill:#dbeafe,stroke:#1c69d4,color:#0b1b33 classDef code fill:#f1f5f9,stroke:#64748b,color:#0b1b33 classDef human fill:#ffedd5,stroke:#ea580c,color:#3b1a05 class F,R,W ai class E,S,V,P,A code class D human ``` Blue is where the AI works, grey is plain code, orange is where a person decides. The numbers are the real ones for the BMW 5 Series (G60) in the US. | Step | What happens | Who does it | |---|---|---| | 1. Read | Comments, study, sales and option list become *evidence*, each with a stable ID | Code | | 2. Find patterns | Evidence is grouped into *findings*: complaints, unmet needs, things people love | AI, citing evidence IDs | | 3. Check outside | Competitor strengths and trends from the web, each with URL, date and a trust level | AI + rules | | 4. Write requirements | Findings become customer-facing, measurable requirements with assumptions | AI drafts, all start as `proposed` | | 5. Rank | Weighted formula: customer pain, reach, satisfaction gap, competition, future relevance, effort | Python, no AI | | 6. Decide | Approve, reject, edit or challenge. A reason is required | **Only the PM** | | 7. Log | Every change is stored with who, when, why, before and after, in a SHA-256 hash chain | Code | --- ## A tour through the product ### 1. The ranked list The cockpit shows what the successor should do better, ranked by customer evidence. The traffic light next to each row tells you in one glance how solid it is: green is proven, yellow is weak, red is an assumption. ![Cockpit with the ranked requirements for the BMW 5 Series (G60) US](docs/images/cockpit.png) ### 2. Ask in your own words A PM rarely thinks in weights. They think "what matters for families who do road trips?". You type the question, the AI translates it into weights and topics, and Python re-ranks. The AI never picks requirements itself, so it cannot invent one. If you like the result, "Apply" saves it, and your question becomes the reason in the audit trail. ![Ask a prioritization question in plain English](docs/images/ask-in-your-words.png) You can also move the sliders yourself. Nothing is saved until you press *Apply weights*. ![Weight sliders above the ranked list](docs/images/weights.png) ### 3. Why is this ranked here? Click a requirement and the score breaks down into its parts. Each bar is one factor, each factor has a "calculation details" link. At the bottom you see how much the score was discounted for weak evidence. You can redo the math on paper. ![Requirement detail with score breakdown](docs/images/requirement-score.png) ### 4. What customers said, and what we don't know Below the score you find the findings behind it, an "already offered?" check against the official option list, and the assumptions written out. Sometimes the answer is "this already exists as an option, customers just don't know". That is a very different decision than building something new. ![Findings, already-offered check and assumptions](docs/images/requirement-evidence.png) ### 5. Challenge the AI Not convinced? Hit *Challenge* and ask. The AI has to answer with supporting **and** counter-evidence, and both are clickable IDs. If there is no counter-evidence, it says so. ![Challenge with AI answer, supporting and counter evidence](docs/images/challenge.png) ### 6. The audit trail Every AI proposal and every PM decision lands here, in order, with its reason. Each entry carries the hash of the one before it. Change anything later and the check at the top turns red. ![Audit trail with verified hash chain](docs/images/audit-trail.png) ### 7. Honest about uncertainty The insights page splits requirements into "evidence today" and "bet on the successor", and has a tab called **What we do not know**. It lists the weakly backed requirements and the study that would settle each one. | Evidence vs. assumption | What we do not know | |---|---| | ![Insights matrix](docs/images/insights-matrix.png) | ![Insights unknowns](docs/images/insights-unknowns.png) | ### 8. Six models and markets, one pipeline The same pipeline runs for six model/market combinations. Adding one is a JSON file in `config/scenarios/`, not new code. Thin data stays thin: G68-CN has no customer comments, so it shows fewer proposals and says why, instead of filling the list with guesses. ![All six model and market combinations](docs/images/models.jpg) --- ## Can you trust it? We measure this instead of claiming it. The *Benchmarks* page recomputes these numbers every time it opens, without any AI involved. ![Benchmarks page](docs/images/benchmarks.png) | Scenario | Evidence → findings → requirements | Cited sources exist | Quotes match the original file word for word | Top 5 stays stable (±20 % weights) | |---|---|---|---|---| | G60-US (5 Series, US) | 3,867 → 58 → 19 | 100 % | 100 % | 91 % | | F70-EU (1 Series, EU) | 1,570 → 56 → 20 | 100 % | 100 % | 87 % | | G70-US (7 Series, US) | 4,017 → 58 → 15 | 100 % | 100 % | 100 % | | G60-EU (5 Series, EU) | 253 → 19 → 9 | 100 % | 100 % | 99 % | | G70-EU (7 Series, EU) | 154 → 11 → 4 | 100 % | no comments quoted | 100 % | | G68-CN (5 Series LWB, China) | 177 → 5 → 5 | 100 % | no comments in the data | 100 % | For G60-US two of us also checked 50 random finding/quote pairs by hand: 88 % of the quotes really support the finding they are attached to. The method and its limits are in [docs/EVALUATION.md](docs/EVALUATION.md). --- ## Try it You need Python 3.12 and Node 20+. No API key needed: demo mode runs on the shipped snapshots. ```bash pip install -r requirements.txt DEMO_MODUS=true uvicorn main:app --app-dir src/backend --port 8000 ``` In a second terminal: ```bash cd src/frontend npm ci && npm run build && npm run start # open http://localhost:3000 ``` On Windows PowerShell, set the variable first with `$env:DEMO_MODUS="true"`. Or run both at once with `bash scripts/start_demo.sh`. More options, including the online setup on Render and Vercel, are in [docs/DEPLOY.md](docs/DEPLOY.md). Run the tests with `python -m pytest -q`. --- ## How it is built ```mermaid flowchart LR RAW[(BMW files
Excel + PDF)] --> PIPE[Pipeline
Python] WEB[Web search
+ NHTSA + EPA] --> PIPE PIPE --> JSON[(Snapshot per scenario
JSON)] JSON --> API[FastAPI backend] API <--> UI[PM cockpit
Next.js] API --> AUD[(Audit trail
SQLite hash chain)] ``` The pipeline runs once per scenario and writes every step to a JSON file. The backend loads those snapshots, serves ready-made views and records decisions. The frontend only displays: it does no math, so the screen, the CSV export and the pitch always show the same numbers. Five places in the code carry the core ideas: | Idea | Where | |---|---| | The score is a formula, not an AI guess | [`requirements_engine/scoring.py`](src/backend/requirements_engine/scoring.py) (lines 61-70) | | Evidence level A-D follows fixed rules | [`requirements_engine/evidence_level.py`](src/backend/requirements_engine/evidence_level.py) | | The AI may only cite IDs it was given | [`requirements_engine/derive.py`](src/backend/requirements_engine/derive.py) (line 77) | | Every AI call goes through one cached door | [`core/llm.py`](src/backend/core/llm.py) (lines 58-63) | | Tamper-evident audit trail | [`core/audit.py`](src/backend/core/audit.py) (`verify()`, line 138) | The guard against made-up sources is one line: ```python ids = [i for i in dict.fromkeys(draft.signal_ids) if i in known] # drop any ID the AI invented ``` All components, data flow and the design decisions we made (and the ones we dropped) are in [docs/ARCHITECTURE.md](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md). --- ## Documentation | If you want to... | Read | |---|---| | understand the product as a PM | [docs/product/OVERVIEW.md](docs/product/OVERVIEW.md) | | use the cockpit step by step | [docs/product/PM_GUIDE.md](docs/product/PM_GUIDE.md) | | know exactly how the ranking works | [docs/product/PRIORITIZATION.md](docs/product/PRIORITIZATION.md) | | look up a term | [docs/product/GLOSSARY.md](docs/product/GLOSSARY.md) | | see how it is built | [docs/ARCHITECTURE.md](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) | | check how good the output is | [docs/EVALUATION.md](docs/EVALUATION.md) | | run it locally or online | [docs/DEPLOY.md](docs/DEPLOY.md) | | call the API | [src/shared/API.md](src/shared/API.md) | ## Repository map | Folder | What is in it | |---|---| | `src/backend/evidence_internal/` | Reading BMW data, building findings | | `src/backend/evidence_external/` | Web research, NHTSA complaints, EPA range data, source trust | | `src/backend/requirements_engine/` | Writing requirements, scoring, evidence levels, challenge answers | | `src/backend/core/` | Data model, audit trail, store, LLM access, views | | `src/backend/api/` | REST endpoints | | `src/frontend/` | The PM cockpit (Next.js) | | `config/scenarios/` | One JSON file per model and market | | `data/` | Processed snapshots and caches (no raw BMW files) | | `tests/` | Backend tests and the evaluation scripts | ## Data and privacy The confidential BMW raw files are **not** in this repository. The app runs from the processed snapshots in `data/processed/` and the cached AI answers. Without the raw files, only the list-price reference from the option list shows "unavailable". API keys stay in `.env`, decisions stay in your local `data/audit.db`. Details in [data/README.md](data/README.md). ## What it does not do (yet) - There is no login. The person deciding types their name. In production that would come from SSO. - One backend process per audit database. It is a prototype, not a multi-user server. - The 88 % quote check was done with AI suggestions that humans reviewed, not blind labeling. - Thin scenarios (G68-CN, G70-EU) are honest but not very useful yet. They need more data, not more AI. ## Team Piyush (lead, integration, web evidence), Aditya (internal evidence, evaluation), Dennis (requirements and prioritization), Lasse (PM cockpit). Built with Claude Code, sessions recorded with Entire.

# Evaluation

A tool that ranks requirements for a car that ships in 2030 has to earn trust. "The AI looked
good in the demo" is not enough. So we measured what we could, and we wrote down what we could not.

## What we measure

| Check | Question it answers | Target |
|---|---|---|
| Grounding (findings) | Does every evidence ID a finding cites actually exist? | 100 % |
| Grounding (requirements) | Does every finding ID a requirement cites actually exist? | 100 % |
| Verbatim quotes | Is every quoted customer comment word for word in the original Excel file? | 100 % |
| Finding fidelity | Does the quoted comment really support what the finding says? Checked by people | ≥ 80 % |
| Coverage | How many in-scope comments ended up in at least one finding? | for orientation |
| Number in criterion | Does the acceptance criterion contain a number? | ≥ 80 % |
| Rank stability | If every weight moves by up to ±20 %, how much of the top 5 survives? (200 runs) | ≥ 80 % |

## Results for all six scenarios

| Scenario | Evidence → findings → requirements | Grounding | Verbatim | Coverage | Number in criterion | Top 5 stable |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| G60-US (5 Series, US) | 3,867 → 58 → 19 | 100 % | 100 % | 41.8 % | 100 % | 91 % |
| F70-EU (1 Series, EU) | 1,570 → 56 → 20 | 100 % | 100 % | 72.5 % | 100 % | 87 % |
| G70-US (7 Series, US) | 4,017 → 58 → 15 | 100 % | 100 % | 40.3 % | 100 % | 100 % |
| G60-EU (5 Series, EU) | 253 → 19 → 9 | 100 % | 100 % | 50.5 % | 100 % | 99 % |
| G70-EU (7 Series, EU) | 154 → 11 → 4 | 100 % | n/a | 0 % | 100 % | 100 % |
| G68-CN (5 Series LWB, China) | 177 → 5 → 5 | 100 % | n/a | n/a | 100 % | 100 % |

"Grounding" combines both grounding checks; both are 100 % everywhere.
Finding fidelity was measured for G60-US: **88 %** (44 of 50 pairs).

The per-scenario reports are generated, not written by hand:
[`tests/eval/REPORT.md`](../tests/eval/REPORT.md) (G60-US with fidelity) and
`tests/eval/REPORT-<scenario>.md` for the rest.

## How finding fidelity was measured

We drew 50 random pairs of (finding, quoted comment) with seed 42. For each pair the question was:
*does this comment support what the finding says?*

We are open about how it went. Claude suggested yes or no with a short reason for each pair.
Aditya went through all 50 and confirmed or corrected them. A second round, with Lasse checking
all 50 lines, also came out at 88 %, with partly different "no" cases. So the number is not
just the AI grading itself, but it is not a blind human label either.

## Limits

- **50 pairs is small.** Read 88 % as "roughly nine in ten", not as a precise figure.
- **Anchoring.** People reviewing AI suggestions tend to agree with them. A blind second label would be the next step.
- **Grounding says the source exists, not that the conclusion is right.** That is what fidelity is for.
- **"Number in criterion" is a syntax check.** It does not prove the number makes sense.
- **Coverage below 100 % is on purpose.** Topics without a BMW category and groups under 5 mentions are dropped.
- **Thin scenarios are thin.** G68-CN has no customer comments at all, G70-EU only 19. Their requirements rest on
  the study. We show that instead of padding the list.
- **Weights are a judgment call.** The defaults are our best guess. That is why the PM can change them, and why
  rank stability is measured.

## What else we checked

- Python test suite: `python -m pytest -q` (over 450 tests, including the cases below).
- `scripts/verify_stack.py`: loads all six scenarios through the API, runs PM actions, exports
  three formats, checks the audit chain and a full restart replay. Uses a temporary audit DB.
- `scripts/check_bundles.py`: rule checks on every snapshot in `data/processed/`.
- Frontend: lint, production build and the JavaScript unit tests.

Edge cases we found and fixed along the way, each with a regression test:

- A reason made of only spaces was accepted. Input is now trimmed first.
- A failed audit write could already change the PM state. State now changes only after the audit entry is stored.
- Two parallel writers could get the same predecessor hash. The write transaction now locks before reading.
- A missing pipeline step could pull in synthetic data from another scenario. It now fails loudly.
- Very large weights could overflow during normalization. They are scaled first.
- Missing benchmark data showed up as "0 complaints". It now shows as missing.

## Run it yourself

```bash
python -m pytest -q
python scripts/verify_stack.py
python scripts/check_bundles.py
python tests/eval/run_eval.py all       # needs the raw BMW files for the verbatim check
```

# How the ranking works

If a PM can't explain why item 3 is above item 4, they can't defend the list in a meeting.
So the score in ReSpec is not an AI opinion. It is a short formula in
[`scoring.py`](../../src/backend/requirements_engine/scoring.py) that you can redo with a calculator.

## The formula

```
score = (sum of factor × weight × 100) × evidence confidence
```

Six factors, each between 0 and 1. The weights add up to 1, so the raw score is between 0 and 100.
Then the score is discounted depending on how well the requirement is backed.

## The six factors

| Factor | Default weight | The question behind it | How it is computed |
|---|---|---|---|
| Customer pain | 25 % | How much does it bother people? | Defects and usability problems count more than wishes |
| Reach | 20 % | How many people does it affect? | Mentions (square-root scale) × the market's share of 2030 sales volume |
| Satisfaction gap | 20 % | How unhappy are customers in the study? | Share of unsatisfied customers on the matching study question |
| Competitive pressure | 15 % | Do competitors already do it better? | Only trusted web sources that show a competitor advantage count |
| Future relevance | 10 % | Will it matter more in 3-5 years? | Trends and market growth. This is an assumption, and labeled as one |
| Low effort | 10 % | Is it cheap to do? | Effort estimate: S = 1.0, M = 0.6, L = 0.2 |

The weights are a judgment call. These defaults are our best guess for a premium car in 2030.
That is exactly why the PM can change them, either with sliders or by asking a question in plain
English (see [PM_GUIDE.md](PM_GUIDE.md)). Every applied change is logged with a reason.

## Evidence confidence

A requirement backed by thousands of comments and a study should beat a hunch with the same raw
score. So the raw score is multiplied by a confidence factor:

| Level | Traffic light | Factor | Rule (from [`evidence_level.py`](../../src/backend/requirements_engine/evidence_level.py)) |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | green, "Strong" | 1.00 | 15+ mentions and confirmed by both BMW sources (feedback **and** study) |
| B | green, "Moderate" | 0.85 | 15+ mentions from one source, or confirmed by a second source type (web counts here) |
| C | yellow, "Weak" | 0.70 | Fewer than 15 mentions and no confirmation, or only web sources |
| D | red, "Assumption" | 0.50 | A bet on the next generation with little direct customer data |

Two rules we argued about:

- **Many mentions from one source never give A.** One source can be wrong in a systematic way.
- **Web can lift a requirement to B, never to A.** During testing almost every topic had some web hit,
  and many of them barely touched the topic. A competitor's trunk volume is not evidence for a door lock problem.
  BMW's own data counts more than the internet.

## A real example

Rank 1 for the BMW 5 Series (G60) in the US, with default weights:
*"HVAC controls and vents are obvious and operable quickly, and interior storage is functionally usable"*

| Factor | Value | × Weight | = Points | Why |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Customer pain | 1.00 | 0.25 | 25.0 | Mostly "difficult to use" complaints, 25 mentions |
| Reach | 0.215 | 0.20 | 4.3 | 25 of at most 543 mentions; US is 25 % of 2030 volume |
| Satisfaction gap | 0.60 | 0.20 | 12.0 | 15 % unsatisfied with heater/AC controls in the study |
| Competitive pressure | 0.00 | 0.15 | 0.0 | No trusted source shows a competitor advantage |
| Future relevance | 0.103 | 0.10 | 1.0 | No trend behind it; market growth +2.6 % |
| Low effort | 0.60 | 0.10 | 6.0 | Effort estimate M |
| **Raw score** | | | **48.3** | |
| × Evidence level A | | | × 1.00 | Feedback and study agree |
| **Final score** | | | **48.3** | |

The cockpit shows exactly this as a waterfall on the requirement page, with a "calculation details"
link under each bar.

## How stable is the ranking?

If the list flips completely when someone nudges a weight, it is not worth much. So for every
scenario we run 200 simulations where each weight moves randomly by up to ±20 %, and count how
much of the top 5 survives. For G60-US it is 91 %, and the #1 stays #1 in all 200 runs.
Each requirement also shows its own range ("rank 2-4 in 200 runs"). See
[EVALUATION.md](../EVALUATION.md) for all scenarios.

## Why not let the AI rank?

We tried to think of a reason and couldn't find a good one. An LLM ranking changes between runs,
can't tell you why item 3 beats item 4, and can't be audited. The AI is good at reading thousands
of comments and writing clear requirements. Adding up six numbers is a job for plain code.

# Using the cockpit

A walk through one real session: deciding what the next BMW 5 Series (G60) in the US should do better.
It takes about ten minutes. All screenshots are from the running app in demo mode.

To start the app locally, see the [README](../../README.md#try-it).

## 1. Pick a model and market

Open **Models** in the top menu, or use the dropdown in the top right. Every card shows how much
customer data is behind the scenario. That number matters: 3,610 comments give you a very
different list than 19.

![Models and markets](../images/models.jpg)

## 2. Read the ranked list

**Cockpit** shows the requirements for the successor, best first.

![Cockpit](../images/cockpit.png)

What you see per row:

- **Rank and score** (0-100). Higher means more customers affected, a bigger satisfaction gap and stronger proof.
- **Traffic light.** Green = proven (A or B), yellow = weak (C), red = assumption (D). The letter is next to it.
- **Status.** Everything starts as *Proposed*. Only you change that.
- **Small warning sign** if customer groups disagree on this topic.

Use the filters to narrow it down, for example *Evidence: weak* to see what still needs work.
Top right: the funnel (3,610 comments → 58 findings → 19 requirements) and the export buttons.

## 3. Ask in your own words

Open **Ask a prioritization question** and type what you care about, the way you would say it in a meeting:

> Families in the US who road-trip a lot. What should we fix first?

![Ask in your own words](../images/ask-in-your-words.png)

The tool shows how it understood you (which weights, which topics) and a preview of the new top 5.
Nothing changes yet. If it looks right, press **Apply & re-rank**. Your question is saved as the
reason in the audit trail, so later everyone can see *why* the ranking shifted.

Prefer to do it by hand? Open **Fine-tune weights** and move the sliders. The list previews live.
**Apply weights** saves it, **Reset to default** goes back.

![Weight sliders](../images/weights.png)

## 4. Open a requirement

Click any row. The left side tells you what the requirement is. The right side tells you why it is ranked there.

![Requirement detail](../images/requirement-score.png)

Read it top to bottom:

- **Title and success criterion.** Written from the customer's view, with a number you could test.
  "≥ 90 % of participants change the temperature within 5 seconds" is something an engineer can build against.
- **Why this priority.** Each factor as a bar. Open *Calculation details* to see the exact input.
  The last step shows the discount for weaker evidence.
- **Without future factor.** A toggle that shows the score if you ignore the 2030 trend assumption.

Scroll down for the evidence:

![Findings, already-offered check and assumptions](../images/requirement-evidence.png)

- **What customers say.** The findings behind it. Expand one to read the actual quotes, with country, drivetrain and source.
- **Already offered?** A check against today's option list. *"No, not offered today"* means it is a real gap.
  *"Only as an option"* might mean a packaging decision, not an engineering one.
- **Assumptions and open questions.** What has to be true for this requirement to be right. Read these before you approve.

## 5. Decide

The **PM decision** panel has four actions. All of them need a reason.

| Action | When to use it |
|---|---|
| **Approve** | You are convinced. It goes into the decision memo. |
| **Reject** | Not now, or not for this car. Say why, so the next person knows. |
| **Edit** | The idea is right but the wording or the criterion is off. Change title, description, criterion, effort, assumptions. |
| **Challenge** | You are not sure. Ask the AI a pointed question. |

A challenge looks like this:

![Challenge with AI answer](../images/challenge.png)

There are a few ready-made questions (*"Is this only a US issue?"*, *"What speaks against it?"*) or you
write your own. The answer always lists **supporting evidence** and **counter-evidence** as clickable IDs.
If there is no counter-evidence, it says "None cited" instead of making some up. The requirement is
marked *Challenged* until you approve or reject it.

## 6. Check the audit trail

**Audit trail** lists everything that happened, newest first: what the AI proposed, what you decided, and why.

![Audit trail](../images/audit-trail.png)

- The box at the top checks the whole chain. *Integrity verified* means no entry was changed afterwards.
- Click an entry to see the details on the right, including before and after values.
  A weight change reads like "customer pain 25 % → 23 %".
- Filter by who acted (PM, AI, system), by action, or search for a requirement or a reason.

## 7. See what you don't know

**Insights** (reachable from the footer or by URL) has four tabs. Two are the most useful in a planning meeting:

| Evidence vs. assumption | What we do not know |
|---|---|
| ![Insights matrix](../images/insights-matrix.png) | ![Unknowns](../images/insights-unknowns.png) |

- **Evidence vs. assumption** splits requirements into "safe and urgent today" and "bets on the successor".
- **What we do not know** lists the weakly backed requirements, why they are weak, and the next study that would settle them.

## 8. Share the result

Back in the cockpit:

- **Export CSV** gives you the full list with scores, levels, criteria and status, ready for Excel.
- **Decision memo** gives you a Markdown summary: approved requirements (or the top 5 as a draft), with
  evidence, assumptions and a line confirming the audit trail is valid.

## Tips from our own testing

- Start with the traffic light filter set to *weak*. Those are the items people will ask about.
- Challenge your top 3 before approving them. It takes a minute and you will have the counter-arguments ready.
- Write reasons for the person who reads them in six months, not for yourself today.
- Compare markets (**Compare** in the menu). If a requirement is top 5 in the US and Europe, it is probably a platform topic.

# Glossary

The words we use in the app and in the code, in plain language.

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **Scenario** | One vehicle in one market, for example G60-US (5 Series, USA). Defined by one JSON file in `config/scenarios/`. |
| **Evidence** | One single piece of input: a customer comment, a study answer, a web page, a NHTSA complaint. Each has a stable ID like `EV-G60-US-FB-G60-0292`. |
| **Finding** (code: *signal*) | Something customers keep saying, built from many pieces of evidence. Can be a complaint, an unmet need, something they love, a competitor advantage or a trend. |
| **Requirement** | What the successor must do, written from the customer's view, with a measurable success criterion. Built from one or more findings. |
| **Success criterion** | The test that decides whether a requirement is met. Contains a number, for example "within 5 seconds". |
| **Score** | 0-100. A weighted sum of six factors, discounted by evidence level. See [PRIORITIZATION.md](PRIORITIZATION.md). |
| **Weights** | How much each factor counts. Defaults are set by us, the PM can change them. |
| **Evidence level** | A, B, C or D. How well a requirement is backed. A = two BMW sources agree, D = mostly an assumption. |
| **Traffic light** | The evidence level as a color: green (A, B), yellow (C), red (D). |
| **Assumption** | Something that has to be true for a requirement to be right, but that the data does not prove. Always listed separately. |
| **Conflict** | Two customer groups disagree, for example BEV and ICE owners. Shown, not averaged. |
| **Already offered?** | Check against today's option list: is this a real gap, or does it exist as an option already? |
| **Challenge** | The PM asks the AI a critical question about a requirement. The answer must cite supporting and counter-evidence. |
| **Prompt lens** | "Ask in your own words". The AI turns a question into weights and topics, Python re-ranks. |
| **What-if** | A live preview of new weights. Saves nothing. |
| **Audit trail** | The log of every AI proposal and PM decision, with reason, before and after. |
| **Hash chain** | Each audit entry stores a fingerprint of the previous one. Changing an old entry breaks the chain, and the check turns red. |
| **Bundle / snapshot** | The finished pipeline output for one scenario, one JSON file. The backend loads it at start. |
| **Pipeline** | The offline process that turns raw data into a bundle: read, find, research, write, score. |
| **Demo mode** | `DEMO_MODUS=true`. The app uses cached AI answers and never calls the network. |
| **Grounding** | The share of cited IDs that really exist. Ours is 100 %. |
| **Next-gen bet** | A requirement aimed at the successor's world (2030), backed more by trends than by today's customers. Usually level D. |
| **Thin / cold-start scenario** | A scenario with little or no customer feedback, like G68-CN. Fewer proposals, clearly marked. |

# Running ReSpec

Short version: locally with two commands, or online with the **frontend on Vercel** and the
**backend on Render**, both deployed automatically from `main`. The processed pipeline results
(`data/processed/`) are in the repo, the raw BMW files are not, so Render can start the backend
straight from the repo.

## A) Locally (safest for a demo)

```bash
bash scripts/start_demo.sh        # macOS, Linux, Git Bash on Windows
```

This starts the backend on `:8000`, builds the frontend for production and serves it on `:3000`.
On Windows without Git Bash, use two terminals:

```powershell
$env:DEMO_MODUS="true"; python -m uvicorn main:app --app-dir src/backend --port 8000
cd src/frontend; npm ci; npm run build; npx next start -p 3000
```

You need a `.env` copied from `.env.example`. Without an OpenAI key, set `DEMO_MODUS=true`:
answers then come from `data/demo_cache/` and the prompt lens falls back to keyword rules.

The frontend talks to `http://localhost:8000` by default. If your backend runs elsewhere, set
`NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL` (for example in `src/frontend/.env.local`) **before** `npm run build`,
because Next.js bakes it into the build.

## B) Online: backend on Render, frontend on Vercel

**Why two services.** The backend keeps the PM state in memory and writes `audit.db`. That needs
one process that stays alive (`core/single_process.py`). Vercel functions restart all the time,
and decisions would get lost. We dropped two alternatives: FastAPI as a Vercel function (state breaks)
and baking the data into the UI (no more decisions, weights or lens).

**Step 1: backend first, because Vercel needs its address**

1. render.com → *New* → *Blueprint* → pick the GitHub repo. Render reads `render.yaml` in the root.
2. When asked for `OPENAI_API_KEY`, enter your own key. Or leave it empty and set `DEMO_MODUS` to `true`:
   then it costs nothing, but free questions to the assistant won't work.
3. Wait until it says *Live*, then open `https://<your-service>.onrender.com/health`.
   You should see `"status":"ok"` and six scenarios.

**Step 2: frontend**

1. vercel.com → *Add New Project* → pick the repo.
2. **Root directory:** `src/frontend`. Without this, Vercel won't find Next.js.
3. **Environment variable:** `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL` = your Render address **without a trailing `/`**.
   Set it for production and preview. It ends up in the browser, so never put a key there.
4. Deploy. CORS already allows every `*.vercel.app` address (`CORS_ORIGIN_REGEX` in `render.yaml`).
   For a custom domain, add it to `CORS_ORIGINS` in Render.
5. After changing `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL`, click **Redeploy**. It is baked in at build time.

**Good to know**

- Free Render instances sleep after 15 minutes. The first request after that takes about 50 seconds.
  Open `/health` once before a demo.
- After sleeping or a new deploy, `audit.db` is empty (Render's disk is not persistent). The pipeline data stays,
  only decisions made online disappear. For a jury that is fine: everyone starts clean.
- A public link with a real key means strangers can spend your credits. Set a spending limit on the key.
- Every push to `main` deploys both. A red CI run means a broken online version.

## C) Fallback: backend from a laptop through a tunnel

If Render is down, run the backend locally and give it an https address:

```bash
cloudflared tunnel --url http://localhost:8000     # or: ngrok http 8000
```

Put the printed `https://...` address into `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL` on Vercel (then redeploy) and into
`CORS_ORIGINS`. Downside: the laptop has to stay on.

## D) Images and media

- Images live in `src/frontend/public/media/` (`poster.jpg`, `split.jpg`, `scenarios/<ID>.jpg`). A missing file is not an error;
  the page shows a placeholder.
- The media list is built at build time. Rebuild after adding files.

## E) Checklist before every deploy

```bash
cd src/frontend && npm run lint && npm run build     # must be green
python -m pytest -q                                  # must be green
python scripts/secret_scan.py                        # no keys
```

Then in the browser: open `/`, `/cockpit`, `/insights`, `/portfolio`, `/evidence`, `/audit`, `/benchmarks`,
check the console for errors, and apply one weight change in the cockpit. It should show up in the audit trail.

# API contract

Local base URL: `http://localhost:8000`. Interactive docs with every field: **`/docs`**.
Data model in code: `src/backend/core/models.py` and `core/model_parts.py`. A full example bundle:
`beispiele/bundle_G60-US.json` (synthetic quotes).

**Rule: the frontend computes nothing.** Every number, label and sentence comes ready from the backend.
**A real example response for every endpoint** is in `beispiele/views/<name>.json`
(generated with `python scripts/make_view_examples.py`, so it always matches the code).

> Some enum values are internal German keys (`Chance`, `reich`, `einzeln`, `Lücke: nicht angeboten` ...).
> They are stable identifiers. The cockpit translates them for display in
> `src/frontend/src/components/insights/labels.ts`. They are listed below with their meaning.

## Read: views (pre-computed)

| Method + path | View | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /health` | Status: `version`, `demo_mode`, `scenarios` | `views/health.json` |
| `GET /api/scenarios` | Scenario picker: scenario + `data_coverage`, `badge` (`reich` = rich / `dünn` = thin / `Kaltstart` = cold start), `headline_numbers`, `warnings` | `views/scenarios.json` |
| `GET /api/scenarios/{id}/overview` | Start page: `funnel`, `top3`, `level_distribution` (A-D), `warnings`, `source_mix`, `generated_at` | `views/overview.json` |
| `GET /api/requirements/{req_id}/explain` | Detail page: `waterfall` (factor, weight, contribution, sentence; last step = evidence discount), `quotes` (top 5 with country / drivetrain / source), `segments`, `conflicts`, `assumptions`, `offer_check`, `web_sources` (by trust), `study`, `robustness` + `robustness_sentence`, `business`, `history` | `views/explain.json` |
| `POST /api/scenarios/{id}/whatif` | Live preview for weight sliders, **saves nothing**: `[{id, title, old_rank, new_rank, rank_change, old_score, new_score}]` | `views/whatif.json` |
| `GET /api/portfolio` | Matrix category × scenario: `rows[].cells[scenario]` (rank, level), `rows[].class` (`plattformweit` = platform-wide / `modellspezifisch` = model-specific / `marktspezifisch` = market-specific / `einzeln` = single / `gemischt` = mixed / `nicht oben` = not near the top), `rule` | `views/portfolio.json` |
| `GET /api/benchmarks` | `quality[]` per scenario: `funnel`, `metrics[]` (`key`, `value` in %, `target`, `ok`, `explain`); `market[]` US only: `range[]` (EPA km, kWh/100 km, rank), `range_gap_km`, `complaints[]` (NHTSA), `limits` | none |
| `GET /api/compare?a=G60-US&b=G60-EU` | Market comparison: same category side by side, `rank_diff`, dissatisfaction, `sentence` | `views/compare.json` |
| `GET /api/scenarios/{id}/opportunities` | Opportunity map: `points[]` with `importance`, `dissatisfaction`, `quadrant` (`Chance` = opportunity / `Stärke halten` = keep strength / `Beobachten` = watch / `Nebensache` = minor), `thresholds` | `views/opportunities.json` |
| `GET /api/scenarios/{id}/trends` | Trend radar: `rings` (today, successor year), `items[]` (`kind`: `trend` or `bet`) | `views/trends.json` |
| `GET /api/scenarios/{id}/gaps` | "What we do not know": `weak_requirements` (C/D with `why`, `next_study`), `missing_sources`, `share_weak` | `views/gaps.json` |
| `GET /api/scenarios/{id}/evidence?signal=&segment=engine:BEV&q=&page=1&size=20` | Evidence browser, filtered and paged: `{total, page, size, items}` | `views/evidence.json` |
| `GET /api/audit/timeline?scenario_id=&requirement_id=` | Audit trail as sentences: `sentence`, `actor`, `rationale` | `views/audit_timeline.json` |
| `GET /api/scenarios/{id}/matrix` | Matrix today/future × evidence: `items[req_id]` with `horizon`, `evidence_level`, `quadrant` (`Sicher & dringend` = safe and urgent / `Belegte Zukunftswette` = evidenced future bet / `Schwach belegt, heute` = weak, today / `Annahme – beobachten` = assumption, watch), `offer_gap` + `offer_gap_label` (`Lücke: nicht angeboten` = gap, not offered / `nur optional` = optional only / `Serie` = standard) | `views/matrix.json` |
| `GET /api/requirements/{req_id}/counterparts` | Same requirement in other scenarios: per scenario `match` (`id`, `rank`, `score`) or `null` + `sentence`. Rule: same category and title Jaccard ≥ 0.3 | `views/counterparts.json` |
| `GET /api/scenarios/{id}/memo` | Decision memo as **Markdown** (text/plain): approved requirements (otherwise top 5 as draft), score, level, evidence, assumptions, line "audit trail valid, N events" | none |

## Prompt lens: `POST /api/scenarios/{id}/lens`

```json
{"question": "Families in the US, focus on charging and space", "actor": "pm.demo"}
```

Response: `{question, interpretation, source ("ai"|"rules"), weights, filters: {categories, only_gaps}, note, top: [{requirement, lens_score, lens_rank, reasons: [{factor, contribution, sentence}]}]}` (example `views/lens.json`).
The AI only returns weights and filters, never IDs. Python computes the top 5 on copies; **the store is not changed**.
Writes `AI_LENS_SUGGESTED` to the audit trail. "Apply weights" = `PUT /weights` with the `weights` from the response
and the question as `rationale`. Errors: `404` unknown scenario, `422` empty question.

## Assistant: `POST /api/ask`

```json
{"question": "What matters most for families?", "actor": "pm.demo"}
```

Response: `{question, source ("ai"|"rules"), interpretation, answer, top: [{scenario_id, requirement_id, title, rank, score, lens_score, evidence_level, signal_ids, evidence_ids, reasons}]}` (example `views/ask.json`).
Interprets the question **once** (lens, one LLM call) and applies it to **all** scenarios (top 2 each, at most 6).
Only IDs from the store, nothing is saved (no audit entry, because nothing is proposed). Errors: `422` empty question.

## Read: raw data

| Method + path | Response |
|---|---|
| `GET /api/scenarios/{id}/funnel` | `{"evidence": 3610, "signals": 58, "requirements": 19, "approved": 0}` |
| `GET /api/scenarios/{id}/signals` | `[Signal]` |
| `GET /api/scenarios/{id}/requirements` | `[Requirement]` sorted by `rank` |
| `GET /api/requirements/{req_id}` | `{"requirement", "signals", "evidence", "history"}` |
| `GET /api/scenarios/{id}/product-context` | Reference from the option list: `source`, `reference_market` (Germany), `currency` (EUR), `min_eur`, `max_eur`, `pages`, `engines`, `note`. Gross list prices incl. 19 % VAT, without delivery. Missing prices stay `null`. Not a US/CN price and not a cost estimate for the successor. Changes neither scores nor the audit trail |
| `GET /api/audit?scenario_id=&requirement_id=` | `[AuditEvent]` in order |
| `GET /api/audit/verify` | `{"valid": true, "broken_at_seq": null, "checked": 12}` |
| `GET /api/scenarios/{id}/export?format=csv\|json\|md` | CSV (`;`), JSON list, or a Markdown spec with criteria, evidence, assumptions and uncertainties |

## Write (every action creates an audit event, a reason is required)

### `POST /api/requirements/{req_id}/decision`

```json
{"action": "approve", "actor": "pm.demo", "rationale": "Feedback and study agree"}
{"action": "reject", "actor": "pm.demo", "rationale": "Too few mentions, revisit next year"}
{"action": "edit", "actor": "pm.demo", "rationale": "Sharpened the criterion",
 "changes": {"acceptance_criterion": "Volume and temperature blind in one move", "effort": "S"}}
{"action": "challenge", "actor": "pm.demo", "rationale": "Double check",
 "question": "Is this just a habit of older customers?"}
```

Editable: `title, description, acceptance_criterion, effort, assumptions, uncertainties`.
Response: `{"requirement": Requirement, "ai_answer": null | {"answer", "supporting_evidence_ids", "counter_evidence_ids", "suggested_change"}}`.
Errors: `404` unknown ID, `422` empty reason or wrong fields.

### `PUT /api/scenarios/{id}/weights` (the "Apply" button)

```json
{"weights": {"future_relevance": 0.3, "customer_pain": 0.2}, "actor": "pm.demo",
 "rationale": "Successor launches 2030, the future counts more"}
```

Factors: `customer_pain, reach, satisfaction_gap, competitive_pressure, future_relevance, effort_inverse`.
Missing factors keep their default; everything is normalized to sum 1. Response: re-ranked `[Requirement]`.
`POST /whatif` takes the same `weights` object (without `actor` / `rationale`) and saves nothing.

## Key fields

**Requirement:** `id`, `title`, `description`, `acceptance_criterion`, `category`, `signal_ids`, `score` (0-100), `rank`,
`score_breakdown` (`{factor: {value, weight, contribution, explanation}}`), `rationale`, `evidence_level` (`A|B|C|D`),
`assumptions`, `uncertainties`, `offer_check`, `effort` (`S|M|L`), `status`, `version`,
`horizon` (`today|next_gen`), `robustness` (`{rank_min, rank_max, top3_share, runs}` or null),
`segment_conflicts` (`[{dimension, segment_a, segment_b, statement, a_count, b_count, evidence_ids}]`),
`business` (`{volume_2025, volume_2030, growth_pct, market_share, note}` or null; null values = "not available"),
`stable_key`, `badges` (short labels such as `robust`, conflict, future bet, assumption).

**Outlook** (default `null`): `Requirement.outlook` is computed by rules on load and also returned in
`GET /api/requirements/{id}/explain`. Fields: `direction` (`grows|stays|fades`), `successor_year`,
`rule` (`category_trend|bev_shift|ice_shift|no_shift`), `assumption: true`, `sentence`,
`critical_count`, `scenario_feedback_count`, BEV/ICE shares (0-1), `evidence_ids`, `signal_ids`,
`baseline_source` (`scenario_feedback|bundle_sample`).
Rule order: a web trend in the same category → `grows`; otherwise at least ten unique negative feedback quotes and a
BEV share ≥ 1.5 × the scenario share → `grows`; otherwise at least ten such quotes, ICE share ≥ 90 % and scenario ICE share
< 90 % → `fades`; otherwise `stays`. The outlook never changes `horizon`, `future_relevance`, score or rank.

**Signal (finding):** `id`, `kind`, `category`, `title`, `summary`, `evidence_ids`, `mention_count`, `source_types`, `conflicts_with`,
`segments` (`{"engine": {"BEV": 42, "ICE": 18}, "country": {...}, "source": {...}, "feedback_type": {...}}`),
`study_link` (`{attribute, importance, dissatisfaction}` or null).

**Scenario:** `id`, `derivative`, `model_name`, `market`, `countries`, `competitors`, `successor_horizon`,
`data_coverage` (`{feedback, study, sales, options, web, external, badge}`), `warnings`.

**Evidence:** `id`, `source_type` (`feedback|study|sales|option_list|web|external_stat|feedback_external`), `source_name`,
`text`, `url`, `retrieved_at`, `polarity` (-1/0/1), `meta` (keys include `engine`, `country`, `source_letter`, `feedback_type`, `trust`, `publisher`).

**AuditEvent:** `seq`, `ts`, `event_type`, `scenario_id`, `requirement_id`, `actor` (`{type: ai|human|system, name}`),
`rationale`, `payload`, `prev_hash`, `hash`.
